text:
alice: quick q — noticed console shows both a "feature flag" toggle and a "rollout policy" traffic slider for the same experiment. who is the source of truth for users hitting the new model?

ben: short answer: currently it's ambiguous. long answer: rollout policy should control traffic routing; flags are evaluated by apps. but our UI makes it look like both can change traffic which confuses ppl. :grimacing:

carol: +1. saw a support ticket where user flipped the flag expecting 0->100% for canary, but the rollout policy still limited to 10%. they thought flag "overrode" policy.

dave: historically we had flags for product gating and policies for infra routing. two separate systems (flags svc vs routing svc). they ended up with different precedence rules. we never documented overlap clearly.

emma: proposal: define explicit precedence and reflect it in the UI. e.g. policy routing wins for split allocation; feature flags can scope audiences used by the policy (audience rules), but cannot enlarge traffic beyond policy caps.

alice: that sounds reasonable. can we show an equation in the UI? like: final_traffic = min(policy_split, flag_audience_share) — something simple so support can explain.

ben: example conflict: imagine policy = canary 10% for model:v2. flag "enable_v2" targets 50% users. currently some requests evaluated flag first and got 50% even though policy should limit to 10%.

carol: concrete snippets help. current flag config we store as JSON in flags-db: ```json
{"key":"enable_v2","conditions":[{"attribute":"user_id","mod":10,"lt":5}],"enabled":true}```

and rollout policy YAML: ```yaml
rollout:
  name: model-v2-canary
  model: model:v2
  traffic_split: 0.10
  guards:
    min_healthy: 99
    ramp_rate: 1%/hr
```

carol: how to make router enforce policy? either router reads both systems and applies precedence, or we unify config store. both options have tradeoffs.

dave: router should be authoritative for routing decisions. simplest: router reads policy first, decides whether this request is in the allowed split, then optionally checks feature flags for feature-level gating. i.e. policy check -> flag check.

emma: that ordering means: policy denies -> route to old model; policy allows -> flag decides if feature is on for that user. but what about A/B test where engineers expect flag alone to route between variants?

ben: we need two modes: 1) policy-controlled experiments (platform-managed traffic splits) and 2) flag-driven experiments (application-controlled). they should be opt-in and mutually exclusive per experiment id. the console should show which mode is active.

alice: can we detect conflicts automatically? e.g. if a flag name matches an active rollout id, show a warning and offer to reconcile.

rollout-bot: :information_source: detected potential overlap: rollout "model-v2-canary" (10% traffic) and flag "enable_v2" (50% audience). Recommendation: link them or choose single owner. https://console.redwood.internal/rollouts/model-v2-canary

carol: +1 on auto-detect. also add telemetry: a metric that shows percent of requests where policy and flag disagree (router decided differently than flag would). helps debugging.

emma: dashboard idea: show a breakdown table: requested_user_bucket -> policy_allowed? -> flag_enabled? -> final_route. Can also surface counts for "flag-only" vs "policy-only" winners.

dave: API implications: we should extend /rollouts GET to include linked_flags: ["enable_v2"] and /flags GET to include linked_rollout. then UI can present the authoritative owner. smallest change with big UX win.

ben: ops note: we must avoid race conditions on deployment ordering. if infra rolls out policy and app toggles flag later, final behavior depends on who synced last. prefer single source of truth for routing decisions.

alice: implementation checklist?
- detect overlaps and warn (backend + rollout-bot)
- document precedence: routing policy > flag for traffic limits; flags can be used as audience predicates inside policies.
- add linked metadata to APIs (rollout <-> flag)
- UI: mode selector (policy-managed vs flag-managed) + visual equation for final traffic
- telemetry: conflict_rate metric and per-experiment dashboard

ben: add tests: unit tests for router ordering, e2e that simulates flag toggles during policy ramp. add migration plan for existing experiments.

carol: question: for A/B tests we also need evaluation hooks (metrics tracked per-arm). who owns the eval: product team or platform?

emma: platform should provide baseline telemetry (latency, error, cost) and per-arm tagging; product teams define custom metrics. platform exposes hooks to ingest custom evals.

dave: sounds good. last thing: should we provide a "merge" button in UI that converts a flag into a policy (or vice versa) and migrates history? would reduce errors.

alice: love that. ok I'll draft a short RFC with the precedence rules + API change. will ping @ben and @emma for review. thanks all :)

ben: thanks — small follow-up: add a release note so SRE/Support know new canonical behavior.

rollout-bot: :white_check_mark: ticket created: PLATFORM-1428 "Clarify flag vs rollout ownership + UI/telemetry" (assignee: alice)

emma: 👍

dave: :thumbsup:
